A.explanation: Coherence describes two sources with constant phase difference, not the spreading of wavefronts through a gap.

B.explanation: Diffraction is the spreading of a wave as it passes through a gap or round an obstacle, as shown by the curved wavefronts.

C.explanation: Interference needs two overlapping waves to form maxima and minima, but here only one wave passes through one gap.

D.explanation: Superposition is the general principle of adding displacements, not the specific name for spreading at a gap.

hints: Look at the diagram: straight wavefronts arrive from the left and then become curved and spread out after the narrow gap between the two barriers.
Recall which named wave behaviour is defined as spreading into the shadow region when a single wave is limited by an aperture or obstacle.
Check the other words: interference needs overlapping waves, coherence describes phase relationship, and superposition is the addition rule - none describe single-wave spreading.
walkthrough: Identify what the diagram shows: plane wavefronts travelling to the right meet two barriers with a small gap, and the transmitted wavefronts are no longer straight but curve outward.
State the physical rule: when a wave passes through a gap of similar size to its wavelength, each part of the gap acts as a source and the wave spreads out. This spreading is called diffraction.
Rule out the other terms for this diagram: there is only one incident wave and one gap, so there are no two coherent sources overlapping to give interference.
Coherence and superposition are related ideas but do not name this spreading effect. Coherence is a property of sources and superposition is the vector addition of displacements.
The curved spreading wavefronts after the gap therefore match diffraction. This is option B.
